notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware is attached and no hardware run was made. One Gymnasium family driver serves one env_id, so this package implements the card's TactilePush-v1 entry (envs.tactile_push_env:TactilePushEnv, envs/__init__.py:9-13); the card's StableGrasp-v1, TactileRotation-v1 and Insertion-v3 entry symbols are not covered (one env per package). The driver sets env_kwargs observation_type tactile_flatten (an upstream constructor option, envs/tactile_push_env.py:21) because the family bridge carries one observation value and the default tactile_map observation is a tuple; the flat observation is 3 state numbers followed by 390 tactile numbers (envs/tactile_push_env.py:34-36,114-119). The fake backend is the package's own pure Python kinematic stand-in (fake.py): it runs no force integration, rigid-body dynamics or contact model, the tactile numbers are placeholders, and it was never compared with the upstream DiffRedMax environment; the sim backend (gym.make('TactilePush-v1')) needs DiffRedMax, numpy, scipy and torch and was not run. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were raised. Five warnings are the expected bridge-derived ones: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed class only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived numeric inputs (ticks, action.values[*], seed in reset, seed in seed). Only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used and no limit or extension id is declared, so there are no catalogue requests. The risk stays R0 because the device is a simulated world and the card floor is R0. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
